speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us understand your condition, can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) or any changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to check for signs of cholestasis; have you noticed any darkening of your urine or pale, clay-colored stools? Additionally, have you experienced any abdominal pain, fever, or unintentional weight loss during these past two months?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of alcohol consumption, and have you noticed any swelling in your abdomen or legs? I would like to review your recent laboratory results to check for elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin levels. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 460 U/L, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: Your labs show a cholestatic pattern with significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase, which, combined with your ulcerative colitis, strongly suggests Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. To confirm this, I need to visualize your bile ducts; REQUEST TEST: MRCP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP confirms the diagnosis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis given the bile duct irregularities and your history of ulcerative colitis. I will now initiate referral to gastroenterology for long-term management and surveillance. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
